content: Individuals diagnosed with diabetes are at an increased risk of developing heart failure, even in the absence of overt symptoms. Research indicates that diabetes is associated with a higher prevalence of structural abnormalities in the heart, which may predispose these individuals to heart failure over time. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) recommends enhanced screening protocols for patients with diabetes who are considered to be at high risk for heart failure. Specific biomarkers, such as N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), have been identified as valuable tools in the early detection of individuals at risk. Studies have demonstrated that proactive monitoring for the development of heart failure in high-risk diabetic patients can yield significant benefits. These include a reduction in the likelihood of hospitalizations and a decrease in mortality rates, underscoring the importance of early intervention and management in this population.
